note.text: Coastal rulers did not hold one uniform view of European claims. Some negotiated with a power in the hope of protecting trade, land or political interests; some had sought British protection; others opposed the German claim. Bell and Akwa participated in agreements, but conditions and interpretations mattered. Lock Priso of Hickory Town resisted the German assertion. Cooperation by a ruler should not be treated as consent by every subject or as approval of every later colonial policy.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Coastal rulers did not hold one uniform view of European claims. Some negotiated with a power in the hope of protecting trade, land or political interests; some had sought British protection; others opposed the German claim. Bell and Akwa participated in agreements, but conditions and interpretations mattered. Lock Priso of Hickory Town resisted the German assertion. Cooperation by a ruler should not be treated as consent by every subject or as approval of every later colonial policy.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A document expressing a wish to retain land or an intermediary trading position shows bargaining, not an empty formality. Later violations of expectations could produce protest. Compare a ruler's decision, the views of other local groups and the power of the colonial representative. Do not force every response into a permanent collaborator-or-resister identity.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask what was sought, what was promised and what later occurred. Name the actor and period. A signature is evidence of a particular transaction, not proof that terms were understood identically or that the weaker side had equal bargaining power.
